 # Seconds to wait before reconnecting after the tunnel drops
 GW_RECONNECT_INTERVAL=30
 
+# ── Go Control Plane (vpn-api) ───────────────────────────────────────────
+# HTTP listen address inside the container. The docker-compose ports mapping
+# binds this to 127.0.0.1 by default (internal-only). Set VPN_API_PUBLIC=true
+# and front with Caddy/nginx for TLS termination when exposing externally.
+VPN_API_LISTEN=:8080
+
+# Public mode — adds HSTS header and stricter security controls.
+# Leave false unless you're exposing the API directly to the internet.
+VPN_API_PUBLIC=false
+
+# Session cookie signing secret. REQUIRED. Generate with:
+#   openssl rand -hex 32
+VPN_SESSION_SECRET=
+
+# Shared HMAC-SHA256 secret for Windows client OTP provisioning.
+# Must match OTPSharedSecret in the Windows client server config.
+# Generate with:  openssl rand -hex 32
+VPN_OTP_SHARED_SECRET=
+
+# How long (seconds) a provisioning OTP token stays valid. Default: 600 (10 min).
+VPN_OTP_TOKEN_TTL=600
+
+# Path to the JSON audit log (all admin actions + provisioning events).
+VPN_AUDIT_LOG=/var/log/vpn/audit.log
+

commits.content:
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SSH VPN Tunnel Server — Environment Configuration
# Copy to .env and fill in your values before starting:
#   cp .env.example .env
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ── SSH ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Port the SSH VPN server listens on inside the container.
# The docker-compose ports mapping exposes this to the host.
# For production, put a public SSH gateway in front and forward here.
SSH_PORT=2222

# ── Tunnel Device ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Name of the tun interface created when a client connects.
#
#   tun0   → for raw SSH (-w 0:0) clients / vpn-connect.sh style:
#              sudo ssh -w 0:0 -o Tunnel=point-to-point ...
#
#   tun100 → for NetworkManager SSH (nm-ssh) clients:
#              nm-ssh uses tun100 by default on the server
#              authorized_keys tunnel="100" must match this number
TUN_DEV=tun0

# ── Tunnel IP Addresses ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Point-to-point /32 addresses for the virtual tunnel link.
# These are VPN-internal addresses, not your real network IPs.
# Use a /30 block (4 IPs, 2 usable) or just /32 point-to-point.
#
#   TUN_LOCAL_IP  = this server's side of the tunnel
#   TUN_REMOTE_IP = the VPN client's side (peer)
TUN_LOCAL_IP=10.10.10.2
TUN_REMOTE_IP=10.10.10.1

# Netmask for the tunnel subnet (/30 → 255.255.255.252)
TUN_NETMASK=255.255.255.252

# MTU — lower than 1500 to account for SSH overhead
# 1340 is safe for most setups; lower to 1280 if you see fragmentation issues
TUN_MTU=1340

# ── Routing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# LAN subnet(s) clients should be able to reach through the VPN.
# This is used for documentation/reference in the summary; routing is
# managed on the client side via: ip route add <LAN_SUBNET> via <TUN_REMOTE_IP>
LAN_SUBNET=192.168.4.0/24

# LAN egress interface for NAT (leave empty to auto-detect from default route)
# Set explicitly if auto-detection picks the wrong interface, e.g.: eth0, ens3
LAN_IFACE=

# ── NAT / Masquerade ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# iptables MASQUERADE: VPN client traffic appears as the server's IP on the LAN.
# Required for clients to reach the LAN and internet through the VPN.
ENABLE_NAT=yes

# ── Split vs Full Tunnel ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# THIS IS A CLIENT-SIDE DECISION — the server always NATs all tun traffic.
# After connecting, the CLIENT controls it by which routes it adds:
#
#   Split tunnel (only LAN goes via VPN — internet stays direct):
#     sudo ip route add 192.168.4.0/24 via 10.10.10.2 dev tun0
#
#   Full tunnel (ALL traffic goes via VPN including internet):
#     sudo ip route add 0.0.0.0/1   via 10.10.10.2 dev tun0
#     sudo ip route add 128.0.0.0/1 via 10.10.10.2 dev tun0
#
#   Windows WSL2 (in admin CMD after connecting inside WSL2):
#     route add 192.168.4.0 mask 255.255.255.0 <WSL2-IP>      ← split
#     route add 0.0.0.0     mask 0.0.0.0       <WSL2-IP>      ← full
#
# The server only needs ENABLE_NAT=yes — nothing else to set here.

# ── Authentication ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Paste your client's SSH public key here.
# The entrypoint automatically adds tunnel="N" permission prefix.
# For multiple keys, separate with a literal newline (\n in shell, or use
# a multi-line value in .env with quotes).
#
# Example (single key):
#   SSH_AUTHORIZED_KEYS=ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1... user@client
#
# Example (multiple keys — use docker-compose env_file quoting or volumes):
#   SSH_AUTHORIZED_KEYS=ssh-ed25519 AAAA... key1
SSH_AUTHORIZED_KEYS=

# Allow password authentication — INSECURE, for initial testing only.
# Always set back to 'no' for production use.
ALLOW_PASSWORD_AUTH=no

# Root password — only used when ALLOW_PASSWORD_AUTH=yes
SSH_ROOT_PASSWORD=

# ── Logging ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# sshd log verbosity:
#   QUIET, FATAL, ERROR, INFO (default), VERBOSE, DEBUG, DEBUG1, DEBUG2, DEBUG3
LOG_LEVEL=INFO

# How often (seconds) the tun-monitor checks for the tun device appearing
TUN_MONITOR_INTERVAL=5

# ── Gateway Reverse Tunnel ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Connects this container to a public SSH server via a reverse port-forward,
# so VPN clients can reach this server even when it has no public IP.
#
# Topology:
#   VPN Client → GW_HOST:GW_EXPOSED_PORT
#                   └─(reverse SSH tunnel)──► this container:SSH_PORT
#
# Requirements on the public gateway server's /etc/ssh/sshd_config:
#   GatewayPorts yes         ← allows binding GW_BIND_ADDR:GW_EXPOSED_PORT
#   AllowTcpForwarding yes   ← allows forwarding
#
# Enable this feature (set to "yes" to activate):
GW_ENABLED=no

# ── Gateway Connection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Public IP or hostname of the SSH gateway server
GW_HOST=

# SSH port on the gateway server (usually 22)
GW_PORT=22

# SSH user on the gateway server
GW_USER=root

# ── Gateway Authentication ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Choose ONE authentication method:

# Option 1 — SSH Key File (RECOMMENDED for production)
# Set GW_SSH_KEY_HOST_PATH to the host path of your private key.
# docker-compose mounts it read-only at /etc/ssh/gw_key inside the container.
# GW_SSH_KEY_FILE must always point to the container-side path.
GW_SSH_KEY_HOST_PATH=/root/.ssh/id_ed25519
GW_SSH_KEY_FILE=/etc/ssh/gw_key

# Option 2 — SSH Key Content as environment variable
# Paste the raw PEM private key with \n instead of real newlines, e.g.:
#   GW_SSH_KEY=-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\nAAAA...\n-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----
# Or base64-encode the whole key file and set GW_SSH_KEY_B64=yes:
#   GW_SSH_KEY=$(base64 -w0 ~/.ssh/id_ed25519)
#   GW_SSH_KEY_B64=yes
GW_SSH_KEY=
GW_SSH_KEY_B64=no

# Option 3 — Password (testing only — NOT recommended for production)
# Requires sshpass (included in image). Gateway must allow password auth.
GW_PASSWORD=

# ── Exposure ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Port on the public gateway that VPN clients will connect to.
# Must be free on the gateway server.
GW_EXPOSED_PORT=2255

# Bind address on the gateway for the exposed port.
# 0.0.0.0   → accessible from any IP (requires GatewayPorts yes on gateway)
# 127.0.0.1 → localhost only (if gateway itself is the VPN client)
GW_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0

# Seconds to wait before reconnecting after the tunnel drops
GW_RECONNECT_INTERVAL=30

# ── Client Connection via Gateway ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# After setting GW_ENABLED=yes and starting the container:
#
#   # Connect from Linux/WSL2:
#   sudo ssh -w 0:0 -o Tunnel=point-to-point \
#        -o ServerAliveInterval=30 \
#        -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 \
#        -p ${GW_EXPOSED_PORT} -f -N root@${GW_HOST}
#
#   sudo ip addr add 10.10.10.1 peer 10.10.10.2/32 dev tun0
#   sudo ip link set tun0 up
#   sudo ip route add 192.168.4.0/24 via 10.10.10.2 dev tun0
#
#   # Windows WSL2 — then in CMD (admin):
#   route add 10.10.10.0 mask 255.255.255.252 <WSL2-IP>
#   route add 192.168.4.0 mask 255.255.255.0  <WSL2-IP>

# NetworkManager SSH (nm-ssh, Linux):
#   Set TUN_DEV=tun100, rebuild/restart the container, then:
#   nmcli con up <your-nm-ssh-connection-name>
